provenance.capture_method: Official BLS HTML release inspected through public web retrieval; normalized facts transcribed into this append-only artifact.
provenance.source_independence: The CPI and Real Earnings releases are separate BLS releases but share one publisher and are not independent publisher corroboration.

year_over_year.missing_reason: BLS could not collect October 2025 CPI data during the lapse in appropriations; October 2025 to October 2026 real-earnings comparisons are unavailable.

confirmed_primary_facts: All-employee real average hourly earnings were unchanged from September to October 2026, seasonally adjusted.
All-employee nominal average hourly earnings increased 0.4 percent while CPI-U increased 0.4 percent.
All-employee real average weekly earnings were unchanged because real hourly earnings and the average workweek were unchanged.
Production and nonsupervisory real average hourly earnings increased 0.1 percent.
Production and nonsupervisory real average weekly earnings decreased 0.3 percent because the average workweek decreased 0.3 percent.
October 2025 to October 2026 real-earnings comparisons are unavailable because the required October 2025 CPI data were not collected.
inference_not_fact: The release indicates no aggregate real hourly or weekly earnings gain for all private nonfarm employees in October, while production/nonsupervisory weekly purchasing power declined modestly.

The real-earnings release does not offset the October CPI surprise: headline monthly CPI was 0.4 percent versus 0.3 percent preview consensus, and core was 0.3 percent versus 0.2 percent preview consensus.

competing_macro_hypotheses.statement: Core CPI at 0.3 percent month over month, matching Waller's stated threshold, may reinforce expectations of restrictive Federal Reserve policy and weigh on high-beta risk assets.
disconfirming_evidence: The headline monthly rate slowed from 0.6 to 0.4 percent.
The real-earnings release shows no broad acceleration in real wages.
Post-release rates, dollar and risk-asset repricing have not been captured in synchronized provider-timestamped data.

competing_macro_hypotheses.statement: The decline in headline monthly CPI from 0.6 to 0.4 percent may be read as partial headline disinflation and could limit a hawkish interpretation.
disconfirming_evidence: Headline and core monthly CPI both exceeded the Reuters preview consensus by 0.1 percentage point.
Core remained at 0.3 percent for a third consecutive month.
Annual headline and core comparisons are unavailable for October.

competing_macro_hypotheses.statement: The CPI and real-earnings releases may have no stable directional XRP effect absent synchronized market repricing and repeated out-of-sample event evidence.
tests_needed: Provider-timestamped XRP/USD and XRP/USDT trades, top-of-book and depth around the 13:30 UTC release.
Synchronized BTC, broad risk, DXY, Treasury yields and Fed-futures observations.
Repeated event study with pre-registered windows, non-event controls and leakage-safe evaluation.

model_admission.reason: The release has not yet been ingested into the point-in-time feature store with a verified raw-source receipt and independent timestamp anchor.
model_admission.missing_values: YoY values remain null; never zero-fill, interpolate or carry forward.
